"""The vision model's slot vocabulary, generated from the catalogue.

DO NOT EDIT. This module is written by ``chip_chat.catalog.vocabulary`` from a
built catalogue and is overwritten whenever the catalogue is rebuilt. A term
here exists because a published menu row exists; editing one by hand would
reintroduce exactly the drift RFC-001 section 07 generates it to prevent.

Catalogue content version:
    0e5eb9c65accf0ff50d77903eab0cba31918157bc21402a88a520240d520a604
"""

from enum import StrEnum


class Vessel(StrEnum):
    """Published vessel the model may return."""

    BOWL = "bowl"
    """Bowl."""
    BURRITO = "burrito"
    """Burrito."""


class Protein(StrEnum):
    """Published protein the model may return."""

    CHICKEN = "chicken"
    """Chicken."""
    STEAK = "steak"
    """Steak."""


class Rice(StrEnum):
    """Published rice the model may return."""

    WHITE_RICE = "white_rice"
    """White Rice."""


class Bean(StrEnum):
    """Published beans the model may return."""

    BLACK_BEANS = "black_beans"
    """Black Beans."""


class Salsa(StrEnum):
    """Published salsas the model may return."""

    # The catalogue published no term for this slot.
    pass


class Topping(StrEnum):
    """Published toppings the model may return."""

    CHEESE = "cheese"
    """Cheese."""
    GUACAMOLE = "guacamole"
    """Guacamole."""


SLOT_ITEMS: dict[str, dict[str, tuple[str, ...]]] = {
    # Slot to term to the catalogue items the term may resolve to.
    # More than one is normal: Chipotle publishes guacamole under two
    # identifiers and white rice under two more, so which one a described
    # meal means depends on the entree it is on. Resolve (entree, term)
    # against the catalogue's `modifiers` table; this is the candidate set.
    # `vessel` and `protein` are empty on purpose: each is half of an
    # entree, and the pair resolves through the catalogue's
    # `(item_type, primary_filling)` rather than through either half.
    "vessel": {
        "bowl": (),
        "burrito": (),
    },
    "protein": {
        "chicken": (),
        "steak": (),
    },
    "rice": {
        "white_rice": ("CMG-5001",),
    },
    "beans": {
        "black_beans": ("CMG-5051",),
    },
    "salsas": {},
    "toppings": {
        "cheese": ("CMG-5252",),
        "guacamole": ("CMG-1001",),
    },
}


def _slot(values: list[str]) -> dict[str, object]:
    """One slot: a value from the catalogue, and how sure the model is."""
    return {
        "type": "object",
        "additionalProperties": False,
        "required": ["value", "confidence"],
        "properties": {
            "value": {"type": "string", "enum": values},
            "confidence": {"type": "number", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 1},
        },
    }


DESCRIBE_SCHEMA: dict[str, object] = {
    # RFC-001 section 07, stage 4. The model may return nothing else.
    "type": "object",
    "additionalProperties": False,
    "required": ["is_chipotle_style", "meals_visible"],
    "properties": {
        "is_chipotle_style": {"type": "boolean"},
        "vessel": _slot(["bowl", "burrito"]),
        "protein": _slot(["chicken", "steak"]),
        "rice": _slot(["white_rice"]),
        "beans": _slot(["black_beans"]),
        "salsas": {"type": "array", "items": _slot([])},
        "toppings": {"type": "array", "items": _slot(["cheese", "guacamole"])},
        "meals_visible": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 0},
        # Display-only. Nothing downstream parses it, which is what
        # keeps the one free-text field from becoming a product name.
        "notes": {"type": "string"},
    },
}
